Our Process

Property & Home Information

You'll provide information about your property and home to help establish the septic system requirements and identify any site-specific considerations.

Site & Soil Evaluation

During our site visit, we evaluate your soil profile, property slope and required setbacks to determine which septic systems are suitable for your property.

Note to property owner: We'll confirm test-pit excavation arrangements and any additional costs before your site visit. Before digging, request a free utility locate through Utility Safety Partners (Alberta One-Call).

System Design & Approval

We prepare a design based on your soil evaluation, property layout and household needs. We'll explain the recommended system and arrange the design permit approval.

Completed Design

You receive your approved design permits, finalized drawings, supporting documentation and system maintenance requirements. Use these documents to compare quotes and choose your installer.

Installation

If you choose us for installation, we confirm the scope, separate quote and available schedule before work begins. Already have a completed design? We can review it with you to prepare an installation quote.

Finding the right system for your property.

The best system depends on soil conditions, available space, and how the property will be used. Common options include:

Septic Tanks

Septic tanks separate floating material and settled solids from wastewater before the liquid moves to the treatment area. Tanks need periodic pumping.

Treatment Fields

Underground distribution trenches that use suitable natural soil to treat wastewater.

Treatment Mounds

Raised treatment beds used where natural soil conditions are not suitable for treatment fields.

At-Grade Systems

An option for qualifying forested properties. Treated effluent is spread over the natural forest floor layer. Requires secondary treatment.

Open Discharge Systems

An option on qualifying properties where site conditions and applicable requirements allow effluent to discharge onto the ground.

Holding Tanks

Sealed tanks that store wastewater for regular pumping, where permitted.

A complete system may combine a septic tank with a treatment field, mound or another suitable treatment option.
